item.title: Maestro 0.9.1
item.description:
The first beta, for people helping to test two Symphony I/O units on one ThunderBridge (64 channels), or a Symphony I/O on a Symphony 64 PCIe card. It contains everything in 0.8.40. Betas may have bugs; if you rely on your setup, stay on Stable.
### Changes that may affect your setup
- **This beta updates the ThunderBridge driver.** After installing, unplug the ThunderBridge cable and plug it back in (or turn the Maestro driver off and on in System Settings, or restart). Until then the old driver keeps running and Maestro shows a banner. - **The ThunderBridge now has a Source choice** in Audio MIDI Setup and the macOS Sound menu: "Symphony I/O: ThunderBridge" (the usual 32 channels) and "Symphony I/O: ThunderBridge 64". Leave it on the first unless you have two units. Your DAW keeps the same device either way.
### New
- **64 channels with two Symphony I/O units.** Connect the second unit to ThunderBridge port 2, then choose 64 channels (two units) under Ports in System Setup › Device Info, or pick "Symphony I/O: ThunderBridge 64" as the Source. Channels 33-64 are the unit on port 2. If no second unit is found, the driver stays at 32 channels and Device Info says why. This has not yet been confirmed on real hardware. - **A Symphony I/O on a Symphony 64 PCIe card should now be recognised (experimental).** With the PCIe card in a Thunderbolt chassis, Maestro showed the Symphony I/O as an "Apogee DD-16X" and none of Maestro's settings reached it. It should now appear as a Symphony I/O with its option cards. This has not yet been confirmed on real hardware.
### For testers
- Please report whether 64 channels work with two units, and whether 32 channels still work as before with one. - If you use the Symphony 64 PCIe card: please report whether Device Info now lists your option cards, whether Maestro's controls work, and whether audio plays and records. If it still shows a different unit, press Copy next to Device Info and send the text. - If you have one of the 64-channel test builds (9004-9006), install this package by hand once. When Maestro next checks for updates it sets the update channel to Beta, and you keep getting betas. - To leave the beta, choose Stable under Update channel in Device Settings › Preferences; Maestro offers to reinstall the latest stable version.

item.title: Maestro 0.8.40
item.description:
Every option card now behaves the way it did in Apogee's original Maestro: the optical format, the S/PDIF coax settings, the clock choices and the channel names.
### Changes that may affect your setup
These work differently from 0.8.39. Most match Apogee's original; check them after updating.
- **This release updates the ThunderBridge driver.** After installing, unplug the ThunderBridge cable and plug it back in (or turn the Maestro driver off and on in System Settings, or restart). Until then the old driver keeps running and Maestro shows a banner. - **Input routing choices saved over ThunderBridge are cleared once.** The Symphony goes back to its default layout (each card's inputs in order). Choose them again on Input Routing; from now on they are kept and put back after reconnecting. Choices made over USB in 32-channel mode are cleared too. - **2x6 card in slot 1 with a second card (ThunderBridge only):** the second card's inputs move from Mac inputs 17-32 to 13-28, as in the original. Check your DAW's input assignments. - **Channel names in your DAW change over ThunderBridge.** Inputs and outputs now have names ("A Line 1", "A ADAT 3", "A N.A."...) instead of plain numbers. The channels themselves don't move. - **Clock Source over ThunderBridge:** "Loop Sync" and the "IO Board 1" / "IO Board 2" entries are gone; each card's own inputs are listed instead. If you used one of those, choose the clock source again. - **Headphones following an output of the slot 2 card** now play that output over ThunderBridge. Before, they played the matching output of the slot 1 card. - **Reset Routing over ThunderBridge** puts back the layout the driver actually uses. With two 8x8 cards, or with slot 1 empty, this differs from what earlier versions wrote. - **The Peripheral Prefix letter is now stored in the Symphony,** as the original did, and is written to it when Maestro connects. - **Optical format and S/PDIF coax settings are now restored when the Symphony connects** (USB and ThunderBridge). Before, the Symphony started from ADAT and the defaults after every power cycle.
### New
- **Update channel: Stable or Beta.** Device Settings › Preferences has a new Update channel setting. Stable is the default and is what most people should use: nothing changes unless you choose Beta. Beta offers versions that are still being tested; they may have bugs and can replace the ThunderBridge driver. Switching back to Stable offers to download and reinstall the latest stable version. - **Maestro reopens after an update is installed.** - **An older Maestro package can be installed over a newer one.** From this version on, the installer replaces the app instead of leaving the newer one in place.
### What's fixed
- **S/PDIF settings for the card in slot 2 now take effect.** "SPDIF Coax 3-4 Replaces" and "SPDIF Coax 3-4 Mirrors" were sent in a form the Symphony ignores, and the Mirrors menu was not sent at all. Both now work, over USB and ThunderBridge. - **S/PDIF settings show what the Symphony is set to over ThunderBridge.** The Replaces and Mirrors menus used to go back to their defaults whenever you left the tab. - **Your optical format and S/PDIF settings are kept when the Symphony is turned off and on.** They used to go back to ADAT and the defaults. Maestro and the USB helper now put them back when the Symphony connects, as the original did. They go back only onto the card they were chosen for, so a card you swap in starts from its defaults. - **Presets keep the optical format and S/PDIF settings of both cards.** They used to keep the first card's only. - **Input Routing over ThunderBridge shows what the Symphony actually records.** The page drew the USB layout (all Line inputs first), but the ThunderBridge driver sends each card's inputs in order: Mac inputs 1-16 from the card in slot 1, 17-32 from slot 2. The page now shows that, and Reset Routing puts that layout back. - **With a 2x6 card in slot 1, the card in slot 2 now starts at Mac input 13 over ThunderBridge,** right after the 2x6's 12 inputs, as in the original. It used to start at 17, leaving Mac inputs 13-16 empty. Every other setup keeps slot 2 on Mac inputs 17-32. This needs the driver in this release. If you record from a slot 2 card behind a 2x6, check your DAW's input assignments after updating. - **Saved input routing choices are now put back when the Symphony reconnects** over ThunderBridge, including after the driver recovers the link. Until now the page kept showing your choices while the Symphony had gone back to the default. - **Input routing choices saved by earlier versions are cleared once over ThunderBridge.** They were made on a page that showed the wrong layout, and the Symphony had not been using them since it last reconnected. Putting them back now could move your inputs without warning, so the first ThunderBridge connection after updating forgets them and the Symphony keeps its default layout. Choose them again on Input Routing if you want them; from now on they are kept. If you used Input Routing over USB in 32-channel mode, those choices are shared with ThunderBridge and are cleared too. - **The software inputs on Input Routing are named after what is routed to them,** as in the original: "A SPDIF Opt 1/2" for a pair fed from the optical input, "N.A." for a pair with nothing behind it. They used to read "A Line" for every row. - **Output Routing over ThunderBridge shows where each Mac output actually plays.** The driver sends Mac outputs 1-16 to the card in slot 1 and 17-32 to the card in slot 2, in order, but the page drew the USB layout, with every Line output first. With two cards that both have Line outputs, such as two 8x8 cards, Mac outputs 9-10 were labelled as slot 2's Line 9/10 while they played on slot 1's digital outputs. With slot 1 empty, the slot 2 card's outputs were labelled as Mac outputs 1-16 while they played on 17-32. The software rows are now named after the outputs they reach, the default the page shows matches what plays, and Reset Routing over ThunderBridge puts that default back. Saved routing choices are not changed. If you used Reset Routing over ThunderBridge with two such cards, or with slot 1 empty, the outputs keep that older layout until the driver restarts (for example when you restart the Mac); press Reset Routing again to get the default that matches the page. - **"SPDIF Opt 1/2" fits on its Input and Output tab strip** instead of being cut short. - **Input meters over ThunderBridge show the right channel.** Each strip used to read the meter at its position on the page, so with an 8x8 in slot 1 the slot 2 card's strips showed slot 1's digital inputs and the Mixer's digital strips showed the slot 2 card. Each strip now reads the input it belongs to, including after you change Input Routing, and the Input tab's digital strips move over ThunderBridge. - **Device Info names the driver build that is actually running the ThunderBridge.** After a driver update macOS can keep the old driver on the card while it already lists the new one as active. Device Info used to show the new build. It now asks the running driver for its build. Drivers from before this release cannot answer, so they are reported as "a build before 123". - **A driver update that macOS has not finished is now called that.** When the new driver is installed and enabled but the old one is still running the ThunderBridge, Maestro used to say the old copy was "finishing cleanup", or show nothing. It now shows a banner at the top of the window until the new driver is running. The banner has one instruction: "Unplug the ThunderBridge cable and plug it back in" (audio stops for a few seconds). A smaller line lists the other ways: turn the Maestro driver off and on in System Settings, or restart your Mac. An Open Driver Settings link opens that page. Device Info keeps the detail, including which driver build is still running. - **Headphones set to follow an output of the card in slot 2 now play that output over ThunderBridge.** They played the matching output of the card in slot 1 instead (for example, slot 2's Line 1-2 played what goes to slot 1's Line 1-2). USB was not affected.
### What's better
- **Channel names follow the optical format and sample rate.** In the Mixer, the Input and Output tabs and both routing pages, optical channels are named ADAT at 44.1 and 48 kHz, SMUX at 88.2 and 96 kHz, and "N.A." where the optical ports carry nothing (at 176.4 and 192 kHz, or beyond the first pair in S/PDIF format, where they show SPDIF Opt). A pair replaced by the coax input is named "SPDIF Cx". The names change as soon as you change the rate or format. - **Clock Source over ThunderBridge lists each card's own inputs,** as the original did: the S/PDIF coax input, then AES pairs or the optical input. An 8x8 Optical card shows "ADAT 1-8" (or SMUX, SPDIF Opt), an A16 IP or 16x16 card shows its coax input, an A16 OP its coax and optical inputs, and an empty or Mic Pre slot shows nothing. A second AES card continues the AES numbering (9-10 to 15-16). Loop Sync is no longer listed; the original offered it only in Pro Tools HD mode. - **Menu names as in the original:** optical pairs are "Optical 1-2" in the S/PDIF and headphone menus, the input menu is "SPDIF Coax Replaces", and the optical format choices are "ADAT/SMUX" and "SPDIF". - **Audio apps see channel names over ThunderBridge.** The driver now names each input and output channel ("A Line 1", "A ADAT 3", "A SPDIF Cx 1"...) for Audio MIDI Setup and DAWs, following the same rules. Each Mac output is named after the output it plays through by default: Mac outputs 1-16 after the card in slot 1, 17-32 after the card in slot 2, so with an 8x8 set to S/PDIF in slot 1 and an A16 IP in slot 2 they read "A Line 1" to "A Line 8", "A SPDIF Opt 1" and "2", "A N.A." for 11-16, then "A ADAT 9" to "A ADAT 24". The names on the Output Routing page are the same. The letter in front is the Peripheral Prefix from Device Settings, which Maestro now stores in the Symphony, as the original did. - **Channels that carry nothing are greyed out.** "N.A." strips, routing columns and mixer names stay where they are, as in the original, but are faded. - **The ThunderBridge driver no longer sends an optical format to an AES card.** An AES card has no optical format to set, and Apogee's software never sent one.
### Release notes
- This release includes a new ThunderBridge driver (0.10.17, build 123) carrying the driver changes above: input and output channel names with the prefix letter, names that follow the sample rate, no optical format for an AES card, keeping your settings after a link recovery, and Device Info's driver build report. - Mac outputs keep fixed names based on their position, on purpose. They do not change when you re-route an output on Output Routing or send it through the mixer. The original renamed each output after the hardware it reached, so an output feeding the mixer read "N.A.". The user guide explains channel names. - The USB helper changes with this release.

item.title: Maestro 0.8.39
item.description:
## What's new
- **AES outputs are called AES** on the Output Routing page, instead of "ADAT". - **The 8x8 AES/OPT card is named correctly** in System Setup > Device Info. - **No optical format setting for a card set to AES,** as in Apogee's original Maestro. - **Clock Source over USB offers Internal only,** as Apogee's software did. ThunderBridge keeps every clock source. - Using the AES port on an 8x8 card: set the card's DIG I/O button to AES, then turn the Symphony off and on again. - **Quit your audio apps before installing.** Audio is interrupted for a few seconds.
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.39)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.38
item.description:
## What's new
- **The Mixer remembers which mix you were on,** and the button for that mix is filled in so you can see which one is showing. - **The polarity button shows the Ø symbol** on Mic Pre channels. - **The Analog Level menu is in the original order:** +4 dBu, -10 dBV, then Variable. - Includes everything from 0.8.36 and 0.8.37: settings that stay put, the Symphony's knobs and Maestro's knobs in step, no clicking after a power cycle over USB, and experimental support for the Symphony 64 PCIe card and older Apogee converters. - **Quit your audio apps before installing.** Audio is interrupted for a few seconds. Coming from 0.8.34 or earlier, the ThunderBridge driver is replaced, so you may need to disconnect and reconnect the ThunderBridge afterwards.
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.38)

item.description:

- **Fixes no sound through "Symphony I/O : Maestro USB" after updating to 0.8.36.** If you are on 0.8.36 and have no sound there, this update fixes it. - Includes everything from 0.8.36: settings that stay put, the Symphony's knobs and Maestro's knobs in step, no clicking after a power cycle over USB, direct output routing over ThunderBridge, and experimental support for the Symphony 64 PCIe card and older Apogee converters. - **Quit your audio apps before installing.** Audio is interrupted for a few seconds. item.title: Maestro 0.8.36
item.description:
## What's new
- **Your settings stay put.** Maestro remembers settings such as speaker mode, dim, mono, headphone source, meter sources and Peak/Over Hold, and sets them on the Symphony again each time it connects. - **The knobs on the Symphony and the knobs in Maestro now agree,** over USB and ThunderBridge, including mute. - **No more clicking after turning the Symphony off and on (USB).** Maestro now waits until the Symphony has finished starting. - **Direct output routing is really direct (ThunderBridge).** Your main outputs default to Mixer 1; choose Software 1-2 to take the mixer out of the path. - **Experimental:** the Symphony 64 PCIe card is now recognised, and AD-16X, DA-16X, DD-16X and Rosetta 800 converters are identified. Both are untested on real hardware; feedback is welcome. - **This update replaces the ThunderBridge driver.** Quit your audio apps first. You may need to disconnect and reconnect the ThunderBridge afterwards.
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.36)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.34
item.description:
## What's new
- **USB Device Settings now shows Card 2 optical format correctly.** ADAT/SMUX and S/PDIF changes now wait for confirmed hardware readback instead of reverting to a stale value. - **First release built from the source code shared in this public repository.** - The packaged installer remains the recommended installation path. Building the complete DriverKit package requires your own Apple signing credentials and approved entitlements; see the advanced build instructions.
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.34)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.33
item.description:
## What's new
- **Playback continues across sleep on ThunderBridge.** 0.8.32 restored audio after wake but then asked Core Audio to restart IO, which some players treat as a stop. On an ordinary wake that restart is not needed, so driver build 120 no longer requests it: anything still playing keeps playing through the wake. (Players that pause themselves when the Mac sleeps, such as Apple Music, Spotify and browsers, still need a press of play afterwards; they do the same on the built-in speakers.) - **No bursts or loops around a recovery.** The card stays muted until the Symphony link has re-locked, and its playback buffer is zeroed whenever Core Audio stops writing it. - **Better diagnostics** in Maestro's logs. - Driver change (build 120). The new driver takes over on the next ThunderBridge cable replug or restart.
If you appreciate this work, please consider donating to the [San Francisco Marin Food Bank](https://www.sfmfoodbank.org/).
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.33)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.32
item.description:
## What's new
- **Driver build 116: audio survives sleep.** Sleep puts the ThunderBridge into its PCI low-power state, and on wake the card's own registers are back at power-on defaults even though the driver survives. Earlier drivers re-locked the Symphony link (so volume and settings worked) but never re-programmed the card's DMA engine, interrupt mask, routing or mixer, so Core Audio waited for interrupts that never came: everything looked connected, no audio, no meters. The driver now detects the reset from the card's control register and re-programs everything before re-locking. No replug needed after sleep. - Driver change (build 116). The new driver takes over on the next ThunderBridge cable replug or restart.
If you appreciate this work, please consider donating to the [San Francisco Marin Food Bank](https://www.sfmfoodbank.org/).
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.32)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.31
item.description:
## What's new
- **Driver build 114: a powered-off Symphony is detected again, and a Symphony that comes back is re-configured.** 0.8.30's driver took flowing audio interrupts as proof the Symphony was present, but the ThunderBridge keeps producing them with the Symphony switched off, so Maestro stayed Connected and a Symphony switched back on was never re-configured (silence with everything looking connected). The driver now reads the card's Symphony clock-detect bit on every sample and also acts on the card's latched "link was down" bits, re-locking and re-configuring the unit whenever it returns. - Driver change (build 114). The new driver takes over on the next ThunderBridge cable replug or restart.
If you appreciate this work, please consider donating to the [San Francisco Marin Food Bank](https://www.sfmfoodbank.org/).
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.31)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.30
item.description:
## What's new
- **ThunderBridge: the driver now watches the Symphony link itself; Maestro no longer polls the hardware every second.** Driver build 113 follows Apple's model: the OS decides presence, and the driver samples the card's own clock-detect bit (every 2 s while the Symphony is off, every 5 s when idle, never while audio is streaming) and re-locks the link when the clock returns. On the developer's Mac the once-a-second traffic coincided with spontaneous Thunderbolt link drops that clicked the Symphony's relays; the new driver puts no steady-state traffic on the tunnel. - **Wake from sleep re-validates the link.** If the Thunderbolt tunnel was lost during sleep or the card shows a fault, the driver re-runs link initialization and restarts audio. Aimed at the no-audio-after-wake report; not yet confirmed on the reporting system. - Driver change (build 113). The new driver takes over on the next ThunderBridge cable replug or restart.
If you appreciate this work, please consider donating to the [San Francisco Marin Food Bank](https://www.sfmfoodbank.org/).
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.30)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.29
item.description:
## What's new
- **No more microphone prompt.** 0.8.26 asked for microphone access and claimed macOS 27 required it; that was wrong. Maestro's input meters come from the hardware on both ThunderBridge and USB, so the audio-input entitlement, the usage string, and the input tap are gone. macOS no longer shows the orange microphone indicator or the Mic Mode menu while Maestro is open. If you already allowed it, you can revoke it in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Microphone. - Still open: no audio after wake from sleep on ThunderBridge while everything looks connected. Under investigation; not fixed in this build. - No driver change (build 112).
If you appreciate this work, please consider donating to the [San Francisco Marin Food Bank](https://www.sfmfoodbank.org/).
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.29)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.28
item.description:
## What's new
- Driver build 112 fixes a kernel panic reported after the ThunderBridge lost power while the Mac was asleep. The driver no longer reads the card's registers while the system is powering down, and on wake it first checks the card is still present before touching it; a unit that lost power now shows as disconnected and comes back on replug instead of panicking the Mac. - Driver change (build 112): macOS asks you to approve the updated driver extension again only if it was not already approved.

item.title: Maestro 0.8.20
item.description:
## What's new
- ThunderBridge: a Symphony power cycle now recovers on its own — "Symphony disconnected" within a second when it's off, back to Connected with clean audio a few seconds after it's on, no cable replug or sample-rate change. - ThunderBridge: a Symphony switched on after the driver started is picked up the same way; meters no longer move after the Symphony is powered off; opening Maestro no longer disturbs a running session. - Software Return: pan is back, no 5 dB drop at center, and the meters follow the faders, pan, and mute as on USB. - Clearer status (Disconnected / Symphony disconnected / Connected); the driver banner opens the right System Settings page directly. - USB: on plug-in, Maestro waits for "Symphony I/O : Maestro USB" before choosing an output. - Input, Output, and Mixer remember their scroll position for the session, without the shuffle. - After installing, unplug and replug the ThunderBridge cable once so the new driver extension (build 110) takes over.

item.description:
## What's new
- Improves Sparkle updating and the manual updater fallback. - Improves ThunderBridge activation, upgrade, disconnect, and reconnect handling. - Adds clearer ThunderBridge diagnostics, including the active PCI personality. - Adds a high-performance ThunderBridge timing profile validated on hardware. - Updates artwork and setup/help guidance.
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.17)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.16
item.description:
## What's new
- Adds experimental support for the original Symphony 64 PCIe card (`pci19c2,2100`). - Shows the active PCI personality in Software Info and copied diagnostics. - Refreshes the connection state immediately when ThunderBridge is unplugged. - Uses the Apogee artwork consistently for the app icon.
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.16)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.15
item.description:
## What's new
- Maintenance release to verify the signed Sparkle update path from 0.8.14. - Continues using the current Sparkle signing key.
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.15)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.14
item.description:
## What's new
- Clearer ThunderBridge setup and driver-status guidance, including power, PC-32, Thunderbolt, Symphony mode, Driver Extensions approval, restart and upgrade-pending states. - USB-only users no longer receive persistent ThunderBridge setup warnings. - Optional monitor/software-return capabilities no longer appear as misleading startup errors. - Sparkle updater signing remains compatible with the existing key; if an update cannot install, install the signed package over the existing app.
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.14)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.13
item.description:
## What's new
- Uses the same outlined PillMenu styling as Output’s Stereo (Out 1–2) control. - Matches the lower blank label-slot height and hover/native menu behavior. - Preserves the verified stereo source assignment routing and existing DAW/Direct Monitor behavior. - Sparkle scheduled update checks remain optional; you can disable them in **Device Settings › Preferences** while **Check for Updates…** remains available.
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.13)
